title: HCN2 rescue corrects otx2 and xbf1 expression after nicotine

fields.label: Label
fields.value: HCN2 rescue corrects otx2 and xbf1 expression after nicotine

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Nicotine reduces or mispatterns expression of the forebrain/midbrain transcription factors otx2 and xbf1 in Xenopus embryos, and Hcn2-WT mRNA injection restores their normal expression, linking HCN2-mediated repair to the known genetic cascade of brain patterning.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 restores marker expression in nicotine-treated embryos

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, HCN2 channel rescue of nicotine-induced defects includes correction of otx2 and xbf1, connecting HCN2-mediated repair of brain to the known molecular-genetic cascade of brain patterning factors.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › HCN2 restores marker expression in nicotine-treated embryos”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos at stage 25, nicotine-exposed from stage 10, with or without Hcn2-WT mRNA

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The two markers and restoration contrast are measurable, and public expression resources can test related parts of the result. Exact spatial rescue under the three experimental conditions likely requires raw in-situ images that are not identified as deposited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify blinded otx2 and xbf1 expression intensity and spatial pattern in control, nicotine, and nicotine-plus-HCN2 embryos, testing suppression or mispatterning by nicotine and restoration by HCN2.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No raw image accession is provided.

Whole-mount spatial patterns may not be represented in transcriptomic repositories.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.93
discriminating power: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.32
data existence: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Domain presence for two named transcription factors is measurable, and Xenbase documents their normal expression. The claim is about the nicotine and rescue conditions, which are not in that database or in any deposited expression matrix. Qualitative images in the article cannot be re-quantified into a test. The perturbation series still has to be produced or released.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare spatial domains of otx2 and xbf1 (foxg1) at stage 25 in controls, nicotine from stage 10, and nicotine plus Hcn2-WT. Restoration is confirmed if nicotine shrinks or shifts both domains and HCN2 returns them to the control pattern; a domain that stays mispatterned after HCN2 would refute that marker.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Xenbase does not include nicotine or HCN2 in situ series.

Two markers are a narrow slice of the brain-patterning cascade.

In situ scoring in the paper is qualitative.

fields.label: Dimension scores

operationalizability: 0.78
data existence: 0.28
